transcript.text: I can help with that. To narrow down why it has stopped working, I need to know if your vacuum cleaner is corded (plugged into the wall) or cordless? If it is a cordless model, did you try charging it fully first?
its corded, plugs into the wall. its a Henry, the red one with the face. no power at all when i switch it on

The two most common causes for this are a faulty wall socket or a blown fuse in the plug (Henry vacuums typically use standard UK plugs with 13A fuses). Please try plugging it into a different, known-working socket first. If that doesn't work and you have a spare 13A fuse handy, check if the one inside the plug is blown; replacing it is safe to do as long as the vacuum is unplugged.
tried the lamp in the socket and it works. i havent got a screwdriver or a spare fuse though. theres some black tape on the cable near the plug, my son did it ages ago

The tape on the cable is a major clue; repairs made with simple tape often fail internally as the wires break or short out. If the copper wires inside are broken, frayed, or if you see any melting, the mains cable needs replacing. If the cable looks fine, we will need to check the on/off switch next.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
the tape is a bit bent there. i cant turn it over to read the model sticker, my back and my eyes are bad. what should i do?

Given that the socket works but there is damaged tape on the cable near the plug, the most likely cause is that the wires inside have broken or shorted out at that bend. This is a safety hazard and needs fixing. Since you cannot turn it over to check the label or easily inspect the cable further, please do not try to unwrap the tape yourself as this could expose live wires. Because this involves mains electricity and a damaged cable, I recommend contacting Henry Hoover (or their customer support) directly for advice on replacing the plug or cable safely. They can guide you to the correct replacement part even without the exact model number visible right now.
